raw_case_text: In February 2001, a 39-year-old man was hospitalized in Marseilles, France, with fever and disorientation. This truck driver lived in Portugal and had been driving in Spain for 2 weeks before entering France. He arrived in France 3 days before admission. The day of admission, his co-workers found him confused and febrile after sleeping in his truck. He had no previous relevant medical history. On admission, his temperature was 40 C with tachycardia, and his blood pressure was 120/80 mm Hg. Clinical examination showed a drowsy, confused man with a bilateral headache, provoked myalgia of the legs, hepatalgia, and conjunctivitis. Neurologic examination showed signs of meningeal irritation, including cervical rigidity, Brudzinski's sign, hyperesthesia, and photophobia. There was no rash, and the rest of the physical examination was normal. Results of biochemical investigation included increased alanine aminotransferase (61 IU/L), aspartate aminotransferase (78 IU/L), lactate dehydrogenase (781 IU/L), fibrinogen level (6.44 g/L), and C-reactive protein (273 mg/L), associated with hypoglycemia (2.9 mmol/L), hypoalbuminemia (26 g/L), hypoproteinemia (54 g/L), and hypocholesterolemia (2.3 mmol/L). The leukocyte count was 11,000/mm3 with 69% polymorphonuclear forms. Thrombocytopenia (110 G/L) was also observed. The kaolin cephalin time was 58 s (control 34 s), and the prothrombin rate was 42%. Blood smears showed no parasites. Cerebral scanning was normal. Analysis of the CSF on day 1 showed 4 leukocytes/mm3, 50,000 erythrocytes/mm3, and elevated protein levels (1.48 g/L). On day 2, another CSF analysis showed 75 leukocytes/mm3, with 70% polymorphonuclear forms, 5,500 erythrocytes/mm3, and increased protein (0.64 g/L). Direct examination by dark-field microscopy of the CSF from day 2 was performed and controlled by two experimental investigators, who observed many spirochetes. The patient received a 10-day treatment with 12 g/day intravenous amoxicillin. The fever decreased to 38 C on day 4 and resolved on day 7. The patient was discharged from the hospital and remained well. No occupational or recreational risks for leptospirosis could be established. The patient had been traveling recently in Spain and Portugal but had no apparent exposure to sources of leptospires.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 39-year-old male presenting with acute high fever, headache, myalgias, and disorientation.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A truck driver residing in Portugal had been driving through Spain for 2 weeks before arriving in France 3 days prior to admission. On the day of admission, co-workers discovered him drowsy, febrile, and confused inside his truck cabin. He complained of severe bilateral headache, provoked calf and leg myalgias, and right upper quadrant abdominal tenderness (hepatalgia).
subjective.past_medical_history: No previous relevant medical history. Occupation: long-haul truck driver. Recent travel: traveled through Spain and Portugal over preceding two weeks; no specific recreational or occupational exposure to rodents, livestock, or freshwater could be established.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reports high fever, disorientation, bilateral headache, severe provoked leg myalgias, hepatalgia, and photophobia. Home medications: none. Allergies: not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Upon admission: drowsy, confused, and febrile with a body temperature of 40 °C, tachycardia, and blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg. HEENT: bilateral conjunctivitis. Abdomen: hepatalgia (right upper quadrant liver tenderness). Neurological: pronounced signs of meningeal irritation including cervical rigidity, positive Brudzinski's sign, cutaneous hyperesthesia, and photophobia. Skin: no rash. Rest of physical examination was unremarkable.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count: leukocyte count 11,000/mm^3 (69% polymorphonuclear forms), thrombocytopenia with platelet count of 110 G/L. Biochemistry: ALT 61 IU/L, AST 78 IU/L, LDH 781 IU/L, fibrinogen 6.44 g/L, CRP 273 mg/L, blood glucose 2.9 mmol/L (hypoglycemia), serum albumin 26 g/L, total protein 54 g/L, cholesterol 2.3 mmol/L. Coagulation: kaolin cephalin time (APTT) 58 s (control 34 s), prothrombin rate 42%. Peripheral blood smears: negative for hemoparasites (malaria excluded).
objective.advanced_workup: Cerebral CT scan: normal without intracranial abnormalities. Lumbar puncture (Day 1): CSF leukocyte count 4/mm^3, erythrocyte count 50,000/mm^3, protein 1.48 g/L. Lumbar puncture (Day 2): CSF leukocyte count 75/mm^3 (70% polymorphonuclear forms), erythrocyte count 5,500/mm^3, protein 0.64 g/L.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Acute leptospirosis presenting as acute spirochetal meningitis/meningoencephalitis with meningism, conjunctivitis, hepatic dysfunction, coagulopathy, and thrombocytopenia. Definitively confirmed by direct dark-field microscopic visualization of numerous motile spirochetes in the cerebrospinal fluid (controlled by two expert investigators). Malaria ruled out by negative peripheral blood smears.
Plan & Treatment: Intravenous amoxicillin 12 g/day for a 10-day course; supportive care for hypoglycemia and hepatic dysfunction.
Outcome: Rapid clinical response with body temperature decreasing to 38 °C on day 4 and complete defervescence by day 7; discharged in good health with full recovery and no residual sequelae.
